summary: For strix's planner (a once-per-cycle JSON-emitting "decide next 1-3 actions" call, not a chatbot), the binding constraint is decision quality and reliable structured output, not raw speed. The strongest evidence (Docker's 21-model, 3,570-case tool-calling eval) puts Qwen3-8B at F1 ~0.92 and Qwen3-14B at ~0.97, with quantization (Q4_K_M) showing no measurable accuracy loss versus F16 — so Q4_K_M is the right default everywhere. My recommended sweet spot is Qwen3-14B-Q4_K_M on a 16GB GPU or a 24GB+ Apple Silicon Mac; the realistic floor for "good pentest decisions" is Qwen3-8B-Q4_K_M (~6-7GB), which fits an 8GB GPU. Models at/below 4B (Gemma 3 4B ~0.73 F1) degrade noticeably and should only be used with heavy deterministic scaffolding. Hardware tiers map cleanly: 8GB GPU = 8B class, 16GB = 14B class (or gpt-oss-20b at MXFP4), 24GB+ = 32B class, Apple Silicon scales by unified memory and bandwidth (M4 Pro 24GB runs 14B at 35-55 tok/s). CPU-only is technically possible (~5 tok/s for 8B) but a poor experience — usable as an air-gapped fallback only, not a target. The decisive lever for small-model reliability is grammar-constrained decoding (GBNF/JSON-schema), which llama.cpp/Ollama support natively and which lets you drop to smaller models without losing structured-output validity.

recommendations.name: Qwen3-14B (Q4_K_M via Ollama) — RECOMMENDED default brain
recommendations.why: Best quality/footprint balance for agentic planning: F1 ~0.97 on Docker's tool-calling eval (top local model tested), strong nested-JSON and 'when not to call a tool' behavior, hybrid thinking/non-thinking modes. Q4_K_M (~9-10GB with weights+KV) fits a single 16GB GPU (RTX 4060 Ti 16GB / 4070 Ti Super / used 3090) or 24GB+ Apple Silicon. Latency for one planning call is seconds on GPU (the Docker eval's ~142s figure was on a Mac M4 Max across multi-round agent loops, not a single call); for strix's once-per-cycle planner that is fully acceptable. This is the model to design strix's prompts and Scope-Guard-friendly output around.
recommendations.integration: HTTP/RPC — already wired: strix's internal/planner/llm/ollama.go calls Ollama /api/generate with Format:"json". Set Model to "qwen3:14b". No code change needed beyond the default model string (currently "llama3.1").
recommendations.language: model weights; served by Ollama (Go/llama.cpp). strix stays pure Go talking HTTP to localhost:11434.
recommendations.maturity: Released Apr 2025, actively maintained by Alibaba; one of the most-downloaded open-weight families; production-grade tooling (Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM, MLX).

recommendations.name: Qwen3-8B (Q4_K_M) — realistic floor / 8GB-GPU + good-laptop tier
recommendations.why: The smallest model that still makes GOOD pentest planning decisions: F1 ~0.92 (Docker eval), near the 14B and close to hosted Claude-3-Haiku on tool selection, with NO accuracy loss from Q4 quant. Footprint ~6-7GB fits an 8GB GPU (RTX 4060/3070, laptop 4070) and runs comfortably on 16GB+ Apple Silicon. This should be strix's recommended minimum and the default it auto-selects on detecting <=8GB VRAM.
recommendations.integration: HTTP/RPC via existing Ollama client; Model="qwen3:8b".
recommendations.language: model weights; Ollama-served. strix = Go over HTTP.
recommendations.maturity: Apr 2025, heavily used, first-class Ollama/llama.cpp support.

recommendations.name: gpt-oss-20b (MXFP4) — 16GB alternative with strong agentic/CoT
recommendations.why: OpenAI's open-weight MoE engineered to fit a 16GB memory envelope via native MXFP4 quantization; built-in function calling, browsing, code-exec patterns and chain-of-thought. A credible alternative to Qwen3-14B on 16GB rigs and worth A/B-testing as strix's brain. Tradeoff: MoE behavior and Harmony/tool-format quirks; permissive but Apache-2.0-licensed open weights make it safe to ship instructions for.
recommendations.integration: HTTP/RPC via Ollama (Model="gpt-oss:20b"); same client path as Qwen.
recommendations.maturity: Released 2025 by OpenAI as open weights; rapidly adopted, supported in Ollama/llama.cpp/vLLM.

recommendations.name: Qwen3-32B (Q4_K_M) — 24GB+ / high-end Apple Silicon ceiling
recommendations.why: For operators with a 24GB GPU (RTX 3090/4090) or 32GB+ unified-memory Mac who want maximum planning quality and headroom for longer context/RoE documents. ~22-24GB at Q4_K_M; runs ~30-58 tok/s on M4 Pro/Max class. Diminishing returns vs 14B for strix's structured task, so position it as 'pro tier,' not the default.

recommendations.name: Gemma 3 4B (Q4) — CPU-only / <8GB graceful-degradation fallback
recommendations.why: Surprisingly decent at ~0.73 tool-selection F1 and small enough (~3-4GB) for CPU-only or tiny-GPU air-gapped boxes. Honest limit: at this size the model WILL make worse pentest decisions, so it must be paired with strong deterministic scaffolding (constrained JSON grammar, fixed playbook templates, narrow tool menus, more Scope-Guard rejection-and-retry). Treat as 'something runs everywhere,' not 'good autonomy.'
recommendations.license: Gemma license (free, permissive for use/redistribution; not OSI-approved — note the use-restriction terms before bundling)
recommendations.integration: HTTP/RPC via Ollama (Model="gemma3:4b"); combine with GBNF/JSON-schema constrained output.

recommendations.name: GBNF / JSON-schema constrained decoding — the degradation strategy (not a model)
recommendations.why: The single highest-leverage tactic for making smaller models reliable: grammar-constrained sampling masks invalid tokens so output ALWAYS parses to strix's action schema. Plain 'reply JSON only' works ~94-98% of the time; constrained decoding closes the rest, letting strix drop to cheaper local models without breaking the plan->guard->execute pipeline. Pairs with: deterministic playbook scaffolding, smaller tool menus per phase, and validate-then-retry on Scope-Guard rejection.
recommendations.integration: HTTP/RPC — Ollama supports structured outputs via a JSON-schema 'format' field (it compiles to llama.cpp GBNF). Upgrade strix's ollama.go from Format:"json" to passing the action JSON schema, so output is grammar-guaranteed, not just hinted.
recommendations.language: llama.cpp (C/C++) under Ollama; strix stays Go over HTTP.
recommendations.maturity: Mature, native in llama.cpp and Ollama as of 2024-2025.

pitfalls: Latency numbers are easy to misread: the Docker eval's ~84s (8B) / ~142s (14B) were multi-round agent loops on a Mac, NOT a single planner call. On a GPU a single strix planning call (decide 1-3 actions) is typically a few seconds. Don't size hardware as if every call costs 2 minutes.

Context length silently eats VRAM. KV cache grows linearly with context: Llama-3-8B Q4 at 32K context adds ~4GB (total ~9GB), turning an '8GB model' into a 16GB requirement. Long RoE/scope docs + accumulating engagement state will blow past an 8GB card unless you cap context, summarize state (strix already has st.Summary()), or enable INT8/Q4 KV-cache.

CPU-only is a real trap for UX: ~5 tok/s for an 8B at 8-bit on a typical desktop (2-channel DDR5 ~89 GB/s). A 300-token plan = ~minute+. It works air-gapped but is not a 'competes with the big dogs' experience; market it as a fallback, set expectations explicitly, and prefer any GPU or Apple Silicon.

Sub-7B models (esp. 4B and specialist 'tool' models like Watt-8B F1 0.48, xLAM-8B 0.57) make materially worse pentest decisions and some purpose-built tool models scored WORSE than general models. Don't assume 'function-calling-tuned' = better; benchmark on YOUR action schema.

Q4_K_M is the safe default (no measured accuracy loss vs F16 in the Docker eval) but going lower (Q3/Q2) degrades reasoning; resist the urge to over-quantize just to fit a bigger model on a small card — a well-fitting Qwen3-8B Q4 beats a crushed Qwen3-32B Q2.
Unified-memory Macs share RAM between OS/apps and the model; a 16GB Mac cannot actually give 16GB to a 16GB model. Budget realistically (8-10GB usable on a 16GB Mac).

Licensing: Qwen3 and gpt-oss are Apache-2.0 (clean to ship). Gemma uses Google's custom license with use-restrictions and is NOT OSI-approved — fine to recommend users download, but review before bundling weights or making it the advertised default.

'JSON mode' alone is not a guarantee. strix currently only sets Format:"json" (a hint). For small models, ungrammared JSON occasionally malforms; without true schema-constrained decoding the plan->guard->execute loop can stall on parse errors.
open_questions: What is strix's official MINIMUM supported hardware tier, and does it ship a hardware-detection step that auto-selects the model (e.g., <=8GB->qwen3:8b, 16GB->qwen3:14b/gpt-oss:20b, 24GB+->qwen3:32b, CPU-only->gemma3:4b + heavy scaffolding)?
Should strix adopt full JSON-schema-constrained decoding now (upgrade ollama.go from Format:"json" to a schema) to make small models reliable, accepting an Ollama-version dependency?
Single 'one model for everything' vs. tiered profiles: do you want one default (Qwen3-14B) or a quality/speed/footprint selector exposed to the operator?

Should strix benchmark candidate models against its OWN action schema (the way Docker's open-source model-test framework does) and publish a strix-specific leaderboard, rather than relying on generic BFCL/tool-calling numbers?

How much of planning can be moved to deterministic scaffolding (phase playbooks, templated recon->scan->exploit progression) so a smaller model is only doing constrained selection — directly improving the CPU-only/8GB story?
Long-context strategy: cap context + aggressively summarize engagement state, or enable Q4/INT8 KV-cache, to keep the 8GB tier viable as engagements grow?
